Built-in color palettes for snake plots

Source: R/colors.R
snake_palettes.Rd

snake_palettes is a named list of ten palettes for the response levels of rating scales. Each palette has seven anchor colors ordered from the low to the high end of the scale; snake_palette() returns a palette by name and interpolates it to the number of levels in the data.

Five palettes are diverging, with a grey midpoint, for bipolar scales such as agree-disagree: classic (red to blue), earth (brown to teal), ocean (red to blue through orange), sunset (orange to purple) and berry (pink to green). Five are sequential, light to dark, for unipolar scales such as frequency or intensity: blues, greens, grays, warm (cream to dark red) and viridis (yellow to blue, colors from the viridis scale).

Usage

snake_palettes

Format

A named list of 10 character vectors, each holding 7 hex color strings from the low to the high end of the scale.

See also

snake_palette() to get a palette with a given number of colors; survey_snake(), survey_sequence() and sequential_dist(), which take the colors through their colors argument.

Examples

names(snake_palettes)
#>  [1] "classic" "earth"   "ocean"   "sunset"  "berry"   "blues"   "greens" 
#>  [8] "grays"   "warm"    "viridis"

# ema_emotions has 5 levels, so interpolate the palette to 5 colors
survey_snake(ema_emotions, colors = snake_palette("earth", n = 5),
             tick_shape = "bar", sort_by = "mean")
